clue.text: Service on line, guaranteed to deliver time after time, one hears?

definitions.text: Service on line, guaranteed to deliver time after time, one hears?

parts.words: Service on line, guaranteed to deliver time after time, one hears?
parts.note: a telephone service you ring to hear a recorded voice announce the exact hour, minute and second, over and over

explanation.surface: Someone praises a reliable phone service that always delivers punctually, or so they hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' suggests reliability, but the service literally delivers the time repeatedly. The British telephone time service is famously voiced by a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: The talking time-announcement service on British telephones is known by this name.

clue.text: As a result of his harassing job a star's snapped?

definitions.text: As a result of his harassing job a star's snapped?

parts.words: As a result of his harassing job a star's snapped?
parts.note: snapped can mean lost one's temper or was photographed; a celebrity hounded by a press photographer ends up both

explanation.surface: A celebrity loses their temper after being pestered by someone at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A singular term for one of the intrusive freelance photographers who chase celebrities for pictures.

clue.text: State how Mr Pickwick addresses his servant

parts.note: as can mean in the way that, i.e. how
in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers, the servant is Sam Weller, called by his first name

explanation.surface: A question of how Dickens's hero speaks to his manservant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb ('state how') but is the definition: an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: A state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Ape that's grabbing hand holding last piece of banana

indicators.note: grabbing says the first piece clutches the rest inside it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

indicators.note: holding means the hand word encloses the next letter

parts.note: a mitt is slang for a hand

indicators.note: the last piece of the word banana is its final letter

explanation.surface: A monkey clutching a banana with its paw holds on to the last bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' and 'banana' paint a monkey, but 'Ape' is the verb, copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them.

clue.text: Joyous experience in drag, all over

indicators.note: all over reads the whole construction backwards, as if turned over
in places the experience word inside the drag word

parts.note: to lug is to drag something heavy
to feel something is to experience it

explanation.surface: Someone delighted by dressing up in drag from head to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' turns round LFEELUG to give the answer. 'Drag' suggests cross-dressing but means haul; 'experience' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone full of delight.

clue.text: Soldier about to divide money in reasonable manner

indicators.note: to divide means to split the money word by going inside it

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
GI is an American soldier
ca is the abbreviation of circa, about

explanation.surface: A soldier sets about sharing out cash in a sensible way.
explanation.walkthrough: LOLLY is everyday British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sensibly or by sound reasoning is acting in a rational way.

clue.text: Dog going up in big rocket

indicators.note: going up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dog is launched skyward aboard a large rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going up' reads letters from bottom to top; 'in' signals the letters IGROC sitting inside 'big rocket', which turn round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famous as the Queen's pet.

clue.text: Book about aged road's for the environment?

indicators.note: about means shaken around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Bible is the Book, the holy book
taken as written, the 's a mere link

explanation.surface: A book about old roads is said to be environmentally friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of the Bible with the printed words. Seeing a book wrapped round a jumble of the rest also fits the letters, but then no word signals that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rots away naturally causes no lasting harm to nature, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Singers tot up blunders, admitting number above zero

parts.note: to tot up is to count

indicators.note: admitting says the blunders word lets the number in

parts.note: to blunder is to err, so blunders is errs

indicators.note: above sets the number on top of the zero in this down clue

parts.note: ten is a number
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Someone totting up mistakes owns up to a figure above nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above' puts TEN before O, as in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Male singers with an unusually high, falsetto-range voice.

clue.text: Unfeeling one, monstrous, seizing power

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: seizing means the big word grabs the next letter inside it

parts.note: monstrous means huge, massive
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted monster grabs power.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no emotion, stony and impassive in manner.

clue.text: Film star with support, back in work

indicators.note: in puts the reversed support inside the work word

parts.note: go means work or function, as in a machine that won't go

indicators.note: back means the support word is read backwards

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: An actor with a backer returns to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Greta GARBO was a Swedish-born Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a legendary screen actress of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: Wheat suitable for all, stored in barrel

indicators.note: stored in places the film rating inside the barrel word

parts.note: a drum is a cylindrical barrel
U is the British film certificate for universal audiences

explanation.surface: Grain fit for everyone is kept in a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard variety of grain used for pasta.

clue.text: Friendly feeling once a tiff is resolved

indicators.note: resolved suggests the quarrel's letters are sorted out into a new order

explanation.surface: Warmth returns after a quarrel is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is resolved' rearranges ONCE A TIFF; the surface sense of patching up a squabble hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondness or tender regard for someone.

clue.text: Journal opening full of gusto, with no end of wittiness

indicators.note: full of means the opening word is stuffed with what follows

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

indicators.note: with no says a letter is dropped

parts.note: gusto is zest, enthusiasm

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of wittiness

explanation.surface: A journal starts off enthusiastically but lacks humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of wittiness' drops the final S, leaving ZET; 'full of' then stuffs it inside the opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: An official newspaper or periodical, often used in newspaper titles.

clue.text: Repetitious slogan, after a fashion almost incisive

indicators.note: after puts the slogan following the trimmed fashion word
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trend is a fashion
a chant is a slogan repeated over and over

explanation.surface: A repeated slogan, in a way, almost makes a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TREND to TREN; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean sharply cutting and forceful in expression.

clue.text: Note supplied with ring omitting first name of jeweller

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: omitting first means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a ring is a clique, a tight group

explanation.surface: A note is attached to a ring, though the jeweller's first name is left off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests jewellery but means a closed group, CLIQUE. René Lalique was a French glass and jewellery designer.
explanation.definitionFit: René Lalique was a celebrated French Art Nouveau jewellery and glass designer.

clue.text: Most peculiar expedition brought about trouble on island

indicators.note: brought about means the expedition word is brought round the following letters

parts.note: a quest is an expedition in search of something
to irk is to trouble or annoy

explanation.surface: An expedition ran into trouble on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the most oddities or eccentricities; the strangest.

clue.text: Birds sat bedraggled around rocky cove

indicators.note: around means the first jumble surrounds the second
bedraggled means messed up, so the letters are disordered
rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Soaked birds perch around a stony inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedraggled' makes A..TS and 'rocky' makes VOCE, which 'around' puts in the middle. 'Birds sat' tempts a surface reading; only 'Birds' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Black-and-white wading birds with upturned bills.

clue.text: Tried hard, torn apart, to follow saint

indicators.note: to follow puts the torn word after the saint

parts.note: riven means split or torn apart

explanation.surface: A saint's follower has been torn apart by effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of strive: made a great effort.

clue.text: Pen shown by catalogue-a good writer?

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A pen featured in a catalogue might suit a fine writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' seems a writing tool but is the pig's enclosure. The definition is cryptic: someone who writes with style.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer admired for an elegant prose manner; the question mark marks the playful reading.

clue.text: Marine creature from south, mostly green and soft

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: green means inexperienced, callow
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A sea creature from the south, largely green and soft-bodied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests colour but means callow, trimmed to CALLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve mollusc with a fan-shaped ribbed shell.

clue.text: Evergreen song about gold automobile

indicators.note: about means the song wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a car is an automobile

explanation.surface: An old favourite song about a golden car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' looks like a timeless song but is the tree. Araucaria was also the pen-name of a famous Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of coniferous trees including the monkey puzzle.

clue.text: A month in France, entertaining time for instrument-maker

indicators.note: entertaining means the month word hosts the next letter inside it

parts.note: mai is French for May

explanation.surface: In France one month hosts a festive time for a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona made fine violins.

clue.text: Acquired, with expression of gratitude, knowledge

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
ken is knowledge or range of understanding

explanation.surface: Someone learns something and says thanks for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean obtained or got hold of.

clue.text: Form taken by verb 'to tighten'

definitions.meaning: the grammatical time form of a verb

explanation.definitionFit: A verb's past, present or future form is its tense, and to make muscles taut is to tense them.

clue.text: Head and rear half of lizard seen behind large tropical plant

indicators.note: behind puts the lizard pieces after the large letter
head means the opening letter of the lizard word is kept

parts.note: an iguana is a lizard

indicators.note: rear half of keeps the back half of the lizard word's letters

parts.note: an iguana is a lizard

explanation.surface: Part of a lizard is spotted behind a big jungle vine.
explanation.walkthrough: One lizard, IGUANA, supplies both its head (I) and its rear half (ANA); 'seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

clue.text: Uncouth lout, never tender

indicators.note: uncouth means rough and unrefined, so the letters are roughed up

explanation.surface: A rough lout is never gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like the adjective gentle but is the verb, offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to offer, as to put oneself forward freely.

clue.text: Smart, comprehending IT, and fairly well established

indicators.note: comprehending means including, so the smart word takes the next letters inside

parts.note: smart as a verb means sting
pretty means fairly, as in pretty good

explanation.surface: A clever person who understands computing is doing quite nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' seems to mean clever but is the verb, to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably placed and secure, in a fortunate position.
